hints.TestGenerate: c := make(chan int); go func() { defer close(c); for i := range n { c <- i } }(); return c
hints.TestCollect: for v := range c { out = append(out, v) }
hints.TestBuffered: c := make(chan int, len(values)); send every value; close(c); return c. No goroutine is needed because the buffer is big enough.
hints.TestFirstOf: select { case s := <-a: return s; case s := <-b: return s }
hints.TestWithTimeout: select { case v := <-c: return v, true; case <-time.After(d): return 0, false }
hints.TestProducers: Launch g goroutines that each send n values on one channel, plus one more goroutine that waits on a WaitGroup and then closes the channel. Range over it.
hints.TestFanIn: out := make(chan int); one goroutine per input does `for v := range in { out <- v }`; a WaitGroup goroutine closes out when they're all done.
hints.TestFanOut: Send job indexes on a jobs channel; start `workers` goroutines that read indexes and write results[i] = f(jobs[i]); close jobs; wg.Wait().
hints.TestCountUntilCancel: In the goroutine: for i := 0; ; i++ { select { case out <- i: case <-ctx.Done(): close(out); return } }

quiz.q: c := make(chan int); c <- 1; fmt.Println(<-c) in main does what?
options: deadlocks: fatal error, all goroutines are asleep
quiz.why: An unbuffered send blocks until someone receives, and nobody else is running.

quiz.q: What does the type <-chan int mean?
quiz.why: Read left to right: the arrow points out of the chan, so you receive from it.

quiz.q: When does `for v := range c` stop?
quiz.why: range on a channel receives until the channel is closed.

quiz.q: v, ok := <-c gives ok == false when...
quiz.why: This is the comma ok idiom for channels.

quiz.q: If several select cases are ready at once, which runs?
quiz.why: select picks uniformly at random among ready cases.

quiz.q: What is context mainly used for?
quiz.why: It propagates cancellation signals and deadlines across goroutines and APIs.
